title: The bird on a string
hook: a bird on a string, a mind racing at 1am, and the self that goes home each night
carry: in deep sleep, the self goes home

segments.voice: Yesterday: food, and the ember and the straw. The finest part of food becomes mind. Your line was the mind is made of food. Week three of year two begins.
screen: `FOOD — THE MIND IS MADE OF FOOD.`

segments.voice: Some nights your mind will not land. It's 1am and it's flying through tomorrow's meeting, last week's argument, a thing you said in seventh grade. Every direction, nowhere to rest. And then, at some point you never notice, it stops. You wake up and it's morning. Where did you go? Uddalaka has an answer, and it starts with a pun.
screen: `1AM, AND THE MIND WON'T LAND.` → `THEN, SOMEHOW, IT STOPS.` → `WHERE DID YOU GO?`

segments.voice: Learn from me about sleep, my dear, Uddalaka says. When a person sleeps, they become one with Being. They have gone to their own. He's playing on the Sanskrit. The word for he sleeps is svapiti. Uddalaka hears in it svam apita: gone to one's own. Sleep is going home. Then the picture. A bird tied by a string flies off this way, and that way, and every way, looking for somewhere else to rest, and finds nowhere. So in the end it settles down at the very place it's tied. The mind, he says, is just like that. It flies in every direction, finds no rest anywhere else, and settles down in the breath. For the mind, my dear, is tied to the breath. Here's the teaching under the picture, one of the biggest in Hinduism. Your deepest self, the atman, isn't your racing thoughts. It is one with Being, sat, the reality under everything, and many teachers read this passage as saying that in deep, dreamless sleep you rest in it every night, without trying. Then, at the end of the lesson, Uddalaka says for the very first time the three words he'll keep repeating to his son: tat tvam asi. You are that. A handful of salt will open them in a few days. So, 1am, the mind flying through tomorrow's test and last week's argument: that's the bird pulling at its string. The worries are real, but they aren't you. Underneath them is a self that goes home every night.
screen: `SVAPITI: GONE TO ONE'S OWN.` · `A BIRD TIED BY A STRING.` · `THE ATMAN: NOT YOUR RACING THOUGHTS.` · `TAT TVAM ASI, FOR THE FIRST TIME.` · then, large: `THE SELF GOES HOME.`

segments.voice: Let the mind fly wherever it wants for a few breaths, plans, worries, memories, and just watch it pull at the string. Then let it land: if you pray, on a name of God you love, said softly on each breath out; if you don't, on the breath itself. Each time it flies off, let it come back to where it's tied.
Sleep. In Uddalaka's teaching, going to one's own: the mind, like a tethered bird, comes to rest, and the self, the atman, goes home to Being.
Your line: in deep sleep, the self goes home. Tomorrow, the bees and the honey they make. Sleep well.

howItsDone: Many Hindu teachers use Uddalaka's tethered bird as an image for meditation on the breath, and the Upanishads' study of sleep, dream and deep sleep became a central theme in Vedanta.
